args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 started failing health checks after it was deployed to production (error rate 18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west and eu-west). The same build was already unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. We tried to roll back to v2.3.0, the most recent healthy production release, but it was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined (CVE-2026-4417). We rolled back all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.2.9, the next most recent healthy production release. After the rollback the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and check whether v2.2.9 is missing any fixes that shipped in v2.3.0 before releasing a fixed version without the CVE.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to **v2.2.9** in all regions, not v2.3.0, and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was unhealthy in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate. It had also been unhealthy in staging (as v2.3.1-rc) before it went to production.
- **Why not v2.3.0:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, but the rollback was refused because it's quarantined for a security vulnerability (CVE-2026-4417).
- **Rollback:** I used v2.2.9 instead, the next most recent release that was healthy in production. No approval was needed for it. All three regions now run v2.2.9, the service is healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It explains the failed v2.3.1 deploy, why v2.3.0 couldn't be used, and the rollback to v2.2.9.

**Follow-up needed:** v2.2.9 is older than v2.3.0, so any fixes or features added in v2.3.0 are no longer live. Someone should check whether that matters. The long-term fix is a new release that fixes v2.3.1's problem without the vulnerability; I put both items in the incident.

content.text: v2.3.0 is quarantined because of a CVE, so I can't use it. The next most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.2.9, so I'll roll back to that.
